top_concerns: Over‑estimation of the combined white‑coat/masked probability
Failure to include a transient sympathetic surge due to acute otitis media
Missing anthropometric and renal laboratory data
Lack of out‑of‑office BP monitoring to differentiate true hypertension from white‑coat or masked patterns
review_summary: The junior differential captured the major categories but over‑weighted white‑coat/masked hypertension, omitted a plausible acute‑pain related BP surge, and did not separate white‑coat from masked hypertension. Important data gaps (BMI, renal labs, out‑of‑office BP) prevent firm conclusions. After evidence‑based re‑weighting, essential isolated diastolic hypertension emerges as the most likely primary diagnosis, with white‑coat effect and transient sympathetic surge as close contenders.
